title: Structured logging and privacy-aware context guidelines
author: Priya Desai
body:
Summary
-------
This page defines the corporate standard for structured application logging and the rules for including request context while protecting customer and user privacy. Goals: standardize searchable fields, make logs machine-consumable for alerting and cost analysis, and reduce accidental PII/secret leakage. This standard applies to all services and SDKs that emit production logs (hosted, dedicated, and private deployments).

Why this matters
----------------
- Inconsistent log schemas slow incident response and make automated analysis brittle.
- Unchecked inclusion of request context increases risk of PII or secrets in telemetry.
- Structured logs enable downstream consumers (alerts, cost attribution, ML ops) to reliably parse and correlate events.

Scope and ownership
-------------------
- Applies to all backend services, edge proxies, workers, and ingestion pipelines. UI/browser logs are out-of-scope for this doc (see frontend logging guidance).
- Owner: Observability Platform (engineering). Primary steward: Priya Desai.
- Enforced by: CI lint rules, pre-merge checks, and runtime sanitizers.

Quick reference: required fields (JSON log object)
------------------------------------------------
Every production JSON-structured log entry MUST contain the following top-level fields:
- timestamp (ISO-8601 UTC)
- service (string): service short name, e.g. "api-gateway"
- env (string): one of [prod, staging, canary, integration]
- level (string): one of [DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR, FATAL]
- trace_id (string | null): distributed trace id when available
- request_id (string | null): per-request opaque id for correlation
- tenant_id (string | null): customer id for multi-tenant attribution (see tenant redaction rules)
- msg (string): human-friendly short message
- event (string): machine-friendly event code, e.g. "model.infer.start"
- attrs (object): libre key/value bag for non-sensitive dimensions (see attrs policy)

Example (single-line JSON)
-------------------------
{"timestamp":"2026-01-18T15:22:43.123Z","service":"embedder","env":"prod","level":"INFO","trace_id":"4a1f...","request_id":"r-3b9c","tenant_id":"acct-123","msg":"inference_start","event":"model.infer.start","attrs":{"model":"gptx-8b-q4","seq_len":128,"gpu":"p3.8xlarge"}}

Field guidance and allowed values
--------------------------------
- timestamp: RFC3339 / ISO-8601 in UTC (no epoch-only logs).
- service: use service registry short names (see appendix A). Avoid environment or role suffixes.
- env: controls downstream retention and alerting tiers.
- level: follow semantic logging levels and avoid encoding state in level (e.g., don’t use WARN for throttled INFO flows).
- trace_id/request_id: prefer OpenTelemetry trace IDs where present. If absent, set to null. DO NOT synthesize ids that include PII.
- tenant_id: use internal stable identifier; map external account IDs to internal opaque ids in the ingest pipeline.
- attrs: strictly non-sensitive dimensions (see allowed/forbidden list below).

Allowed attributes (attrs) examples
----------------------------------
- model: model short name (no path or key)
- model_variant
- shard
- sequence_length (integer)
- prompt_tokens, output_tokens (integers)
- gpu_type
- request_cost_microcents (integer)
- rollout_phase (string: canary|gradual|stable)

Forbidden attributes (must never appear in logs)
------------------------------------------------
- Raw user prompts or responses (full text)
- API keys, secrets, and credentials
- Full email addresses, phone numbers, SSNs, or unredacted identifiers
- File contents, attachments, or binary blobs
- Raw system-environment variables that include secrets

PII/Secrets handling and redaction rules
----------------------------------------
1) Prevention-first: instrumentations MUST avoid placing raw text fields that could contain PII into attrs or top-level fields.
2) Tokenization: where textual context is required for debugging, services should emit a hashed token (sha256 hex, prefixed with "h:") and store the raw payload only in a secured, audited data store (not logs).
3) Masking: for structured fields that may contain partial PII (for example, username), emit a redacted version and a fingerprint: e.g. "user.name_redacted":"j****n","user.name_fp":"h:5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99"
4) Sampling controls: if textual context must be logged for a subset of requests (e.g., failing cases), use explicit sampling—only 0.1% by default in prod, configurable per service and subject to review.
5) Secrets detection: pre-commit linters and a runtime filter must check new log keys and values for regex patterns matching known secret shapes (AWS keys, JWTs). Any detection causes surfaced test failures.

Structured vs. unstructured fields
----------------------------------
- Prefer typed attributes inside attrs for all dimensions consumed by downstream systems. Avoid free-form "details" strings for machine logic.
- Human narratives or stack traces may appear in a separate field called "debug" but MUST be escaped and sampled; debug is excluded from high-retention indexes.

Sampling and retention policy
----------------------------
- Default prod sampling: INFO and below: 1% indexed, 100% stored for 7 days in low-cost blob store; ERROR and above: 100% indexed and retained per SLO (default 90 days).
- Retention tiers are managed by env and service: heavy-volume infra services (e.g., ingress proxies) should apply higher sampling.
- Cost allocation: include a per-log token request_cost_microcents when emitting long-running batch jobs to attribute cost to teams.

Enforcement: linters, CI checks, and runtime guards
--------------------------------------------------
- Lint rules (pre-commit): enforce presence of required fields, banned keys, and allowed attrs types.
- CI contract tests: each service must provide a minimal JSON schema file (example: schema/log-schema.json) and a test that validates emitted logs against the schema.
- Runtime sanitizer: a library used in prod ingestion that enforces max-key-length (256 chars), strips values matching PII patterns when sampling is off, and rates-limits very large log objects.

Schema example (log-schema.json excerpt)
--------------------------------------
{"type":"object","required":["timestamp","service","env","level","msg","event","attrs"],"properties":{"timestamp":{"type":"string"},"service":{"type":"string"},"env":{"enum":["prod","staging","canary","integration"]},"level":{"enum":["DEBUG","INFO","WARN","ERROR","FATAL"]},"attrs":{"type":"object"}}}

Library and language recommendations
-----------------------------------
- Use the company-maintained logging SDK (github.com/redwood-inference/logging-sdk) which provides:
  - JSON formatter with required field injection
  - PII-safe helpers (hashing, redaction utilities)
  - Sampling decorator and integration with OpenTelemetry tracing
- Python example:
  from rdl.logging import get_logger
  logger = get_logger(service="embedder", env="prod")
  logger.info(event="model.infer.start", attrs={"model":"gptx-8b-q4","seq_len":128})
- Go example:
  logger := rdl.NewLogger("api-gateway", "prod")
  logger.Info("model.infer.start", rdl.Attrs{"model":"gptx-8b","seq_len":64})

Operational playbook: incident debug workflow
-------------------------------------------
1) Pager triggers a trace id. On-call engineer retrieves traces and then runs a log query across service and time window using trace_id and request_id.
2) If textual context is missing due to sampling, escalate to Debug Sampling: toggle a temporary 10x increase in debug sampling for the affected service (requires approver and audit log).
3) If PII is suspected in logs, follow incident-secured procedure (see security-and-compliance/incident-response-security).

Rollout and migration plan for legacy services
----------------------------------------------
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): adopt SDK wrapper and add required fields to emitted events. No removal of legacy keys.
- Phase 2 (4 weeks): start CI schema tests; run in dry-mode for two weeks to surface mismatches.
- Phase 3 (2 weeks): enable linter enforcement in main branch and require schema test green for merges.
- Phase 4 (ongoing): runtime sanitizer enforced at ingestion; remove legacy unstructured fields after 60 days.

Compliance and audits
---------------------
- Log storage and access follow data-residency and retention policies (see security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention).
- Access to raw logs with potentially sampled-textual context requires an audit approval.

Appendix A: service registry excerpt
------------------------------------
| service | short-name | owner |
|---------|------------|-------|
| API Gateway | api-gateway | infra-team |
| Embedding worker | embedder | ml-serving |
| Model router | model-router | runtime-core |

Appendix B: common failures and remediation
-------------------------------------------
- Missing request_id in a high-throughput path: add request-id middleware at the earliest ingress layer.
- Excessive log size: blocklist large keys at the serialization layer and emit a small fingerprint instead.
- Secret leakage detection in CI: open a ticket with Security and rotate affected keys immediately.

FAQ
---
Q: Why not log raw prompts for failed requests?
A: Raw prompts are high-risk PII and may contain customer secrets. Use hashed tokens and secure payload stores for debug-only retrieval.

Q: Who approves increased sampling for debugging?
A: On-call + service owner (or their delegate). All sampling increases are audited.
